patternStatus: No APG pattern describes an action sheet. The layer answers the modal dialog pattern and the list of actions answers the menu pattern, each item by item in docs/history/designs/2026-09-24-action-sheet-design.md section 2

identity.reason: The family composes the modules drawer composes and does not render drawer's parts. A bottom drawer's panel measures block-size: min(extent, 100%), 24rem at md, and an action sheet measures its content: two actions and a cancel are 200 pixels, and min() takes no max-content. The bottom panel also spans the whole inline extent of the layer, which on a 1280-pixel screen stretches a row of actions to 1280 pixels. The panel's body, close and resizer would be three empty parts here, and data-ui=drawer is an identifier identity.test.mjs forbids this stylesheet to reach
identity.cost: The layer, the scrim, the slide and the footer's safe area are written a second time, around seventy lines, and the two families can move apart. The behaviour the scope asked to share is shared: portal, dismissable-layer, presence, focus and the scroll lock are the same modules drawer calls

wiring.role: dialog on the panel part, in both modal and non-modal sheets
wiring.aria-modal: true on the panel only while modal, which is the only state in which the page is inert and the scrim is painted
wiring.aria-labelledby: the panel names its title part; a consumer who writes aria-label on the sheet instead keeps it
wiring.aria-describedby: the panel names its message part when one is present
wiring.aria-expanded: true on the trigger while the sheet is open
wiring.listRole: menu on the list part, named by the title part like the panel. Without a name a reader moving by widget would reach an anonymous menu
wiring.itemRole: menuitem on a native button, which gives the press, Enter and Space; the role replaces button so a reader hears an item of the menu
wiring.aria-disabled: true on a disabled item, which stays focusable as the menu pattern requires, and on a loading item
wiring.groupRole: group on the group part, aria-labelledby its group-label
wiring.separatorRole: separator on an hr inside the menu, not focusable

keyboard.effect: moves between the two tabbable stops of the panel — the list, which is one stop by roving tabindex, and the cancel — and wraps from the last to the first while modal. It does not close the sheet, which is the departure from the menu pattern: the menu is the content of a dialog, and a dialog contains focus
keyboard.focus: the item the list last held, or the cancel

keyboard.effect: the same, backwards, wrapping from the first stop to the last while modal
keyboard.focus: the previous tabbable stop inside the panel

keyboard.effect: asks the topmost layer to close, carrying the reason escape; refused when escape is none, and a layer that refuses stops the request reaching the layer beneath it
keyboard.focus: returns to the element that held it when the sheet opened

keyboard.effect: moves to the next item of the list, disabled items included, wrapping from the last to the first
moves to the previous item, wrapping from the first to the last
moves to the next item whose textValue, or whose label text, begins with the characters typed within the typeahead timeout

on an item, runs onSelect and then asks to close with the reason select, carrying the item's value as the result, unless closeOnSelect is false or onSelect called preventDefault; a disabled or loading item does nothing. On the cancel, asks to close with the reason dismiss
keyboard.focus: returns to the element that held it when the sheet opened, once the sheet closes; stays on the item otherwise

tabStaysInside.pattern: menu: Tab moves focus out of the menu and closes it
tabStaysInside.answer: Tab moves to the cancel and stays inside the dialog
tabStaysInside.cost: A reader who knows menus expects Tab to leave; they leave with Escape or with the cancel, one Tab away

twiceNamed.pattern: dialog and menu are each named
twiceNamed.cost: A screen reader announces the title twice on entry — once for the dialog, once for the menu

focus.initial: the first enabled item; the cancel when that item has tone=danger, which is the least destructive action the dialog pattern's first note recommends; with no cancel, the first enabled item that is not danger; with none, the panel itself
focus.override: initialFocus names another element, or false to move nothing for a sheet that stands open beside the reader's work; finalFocus names where focus returns, or false
focus.pointer: a mouse or a pen over an item moves focus to it, so exactly one item is highlighted whichever device is driving — menu's model. A touch does not move focus before its click
focus.contain: while modal, from @slotted/core/focus. A non-modal sheet contains nothing
focus.restore: the element that held focus when the sheet opened, or its nearest connected ancestor. Not after outsidePress on a non-modal sheet, because the reader pressed somewhere on the live page and taking focus back would fight them. On a modal sheet the press lands on the scrim, which belongs to the sheet, and focus returns as after the cancel

back.mechanism: one entry of the session history per modal sheet, held by @slotted/core/dismissable-layer; a popstate that leaves it is answered with the reason back
back.reason: a sheet from the bottom edge is a phone's layer, and the back gesture is how a phone leaves one

item.vocabulary: menu's item, word for word, plus loading. An application that renders menu on a pointer device and action-sheet on a phone maps one array of actions to both
item.select: onSelect receives an event with preventDefault; calling it keeps the sheet open, and closeOnSelect=false on the item or the sheet does the same without code
item.loading: the item keeps its label and draws the spinner in its icon box, so nothing moves; it carries aria-busy and aria-disabled, and refuses activation until the consumer clears loading. The sheet stays open, because the consumer that started the work is the one that knows when it ended
item.link: an item whose action navigates renders an anchor through render in React, or is written as a[slActionSheetItem] in Angular; the role and the keyboard are the same

anatomy.root: the layer, fixed to the viewport and stacked with --slotted-z-index-overlay plus the depth dismissable-layer writes. A one-cell grid holding the backdrop and the panel
anatomy.trigger: the consumer's control that opens the sheet, rendered where it was written and never in the layer
anatomy.backdrop: the scrim, painted only while modal. drawer paints it in both cases; here a scrim over a page that still answers would promise an inertness that is not there
anatomy.panel: the sheet, role=dialog, docked to the bottom edge and centred, three grid rows: header, list, footer
anatomy.title: an h2, the name of the dialog and of the menu. Set small and semibold: the title is the context and the actions are the content, the hierarchy UIKit and Ionic draw
anatomy.list: role=menu, the one row that scrolls
anatomy.group: role=group; a run of related actions
anatomy.item: a native button with role=menuitem, at least the touch target tall
anatomy.icon: the item's visual, or the spinner while the item is loading. Its column exists only when some item of the list draws one
anatomy.label: the item's words; it wraps and never truncates
anatomy.separator: an hr between runs of items, role=separator
anatomy.footer: the band that holds the cancel, on --slotted-surface-sunken, carrying the bottom safe-area inset
anatomy.cancel: a native button that asks to close with the reason dismiss. Never disabled, because a sheet that cannot be left is a trap

geometry.dock: the panel is aligned to the bottom edge of the layer and centred on it, with its two top corners rounded
geometry.measure: inline-size: min(100%, var(--slotted-action-sheet-inline-size)), 32rem by default, so the sheet never spans a wide screen
geometry.reach: max-block-size leaves --slotted-space-12 of scrim above the sheet, so there is always somewhere outside to press
geometry.item: min-block-size: var(--slotted-control-height-lg), which the theme raises to --slotted-target-comfortable (44 pixels) under pointer: coarse, per density. A fixed 44 pixels at every width made the sheet a phone's sheet on a desktop, rows of 44 beside menu's 34. Density moves the height, the inset and the gaps
geometry.label: --slotted-font-size-md under a fine pointer, where the sheet sits beside menu's 13-pixel items, and --slotted-font-size-lg under pointer: coarse, where a phone's own sheets set their actions at 16 to 20 points. The mark is 1.125 times the label, so it follows the label rather than the control glyph scale
geometry.scroll: the list is the one row that scrolls; the header and the cancel stay
geometry.safeArea: the footer adds env(safe-area-inset-bottom) to its block-end inset; with no footer the list adds it. Both inline edges add env(safe-area-inset-left) and env(safe-area-inset-right) for a phone held sideways

mount.active: the layer exists only while open, and @slotted/core/presence holds it through its exit
mount.lazy: the layer is built on the first open and kept
mount.eager: the layer exists from the start and is inert while closed

modal.true: the page is inert, the scroll is locked, focus is contained, the scrim is painted and aria-modal is written
modal.false: the page stays operable, nothing is contained or locked, no scrim is painted, and a press outside still closes the sheet under outsidePress=close

open.result: the value of the item that was selected, when the reason is select

drawerParts.reason: See identity: a bottom drawer's panel has a stated block size and spans the layer, and its body, close and resizer would be empty parts here
drawerParts.replacedBy: the modules drawer composes — portal, dismissable-layer, presence, focus — called directly

controller.reason: Ionic's actionSheetController and Ant Mobile's ActionSheet.show return the choice from a promise. The decision dialog and drawer took holds: with state and @if it is three lines, and the close request already carries the chosen value as request.result
controller.replacedBy: const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); <ActionSheet open={open} onOpenChange={(next, request) => { setOpen(next); if (request.reason === 'select') run(request.result); }}>

radioItems.reason: Ionic's role radio turns an action into a choice with state. A choice with state is a field

boldItem.reason: Ant Mobile's bold and Konsta's bold set a weight. The label is content, and a weight prop would be the first in the library

headerClose.reason: Vant's closeable draws a close mark in the header. The cancel is already the explicit way out, and two controls for one exit compete for the thumb

dragToDismiss.reason: Material 3's drag handle and Vaul's gesture pull a sheet away. The sheet that is dragged is drawer with side=bottom and its resizer, which owns the gesture, its keyboard and its threshold

translucent.reason: Ionic's translucent blurs the page behind the sheet. The surface is a theme decision

emptyList.reason: A sheet with no action is a sheet nobody should open; the application does not render the trigger

size.reason: The item's height is a control's, which density and the pointer already move; a size step would be a third answer to the same question
size.replacedBy: density, and the theme's coarse-pointer block

side.reason: An action sheet rises from the bottom edge, where the thumb is. A sheet from another edge is a drawer

popoverPresentation.reason: iPadOS presents an action sheet as a popover anchored to its control. On a pointer device the same list of actions is a menu, and the breakpoint is the application's
